parts.text:
31 What is an electric current?
A
a flow of charge carriers
B
a flow of energy
C
an electron
D
the charge on a particle

hints: Notice the wording asks what the current itself is, not what it carries around a circuit.
Recall the definition $I = Q/t$, where $Q$ is charge passing a point in time $t$ with unit ampere.
Compare a flow of something with a single particle or a property of a particle to see which matches rate of flow of charge.
walkthrough: Identify the key idea: the question tests the definition of electric current, not power or charge.
State the governing relation: $I = Q/t$, so current is rate of flow of charge measured in amperes.
Charge carriers depend on the material: electrons in metals, ions in electrolytes, electrons and holes in semiconductors.
Options C and D describe a single electron and the charge on a particle, which are particles or properties, not a flow.
Option B describes energy flow, which is power transfer $P = VI$, not current itself.
Only a flow of charge carriers matches $I = Q/t$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Current is the rate of flow of charge, so it is a flow of charge carriers such as electrons or ions.

B.explanation: Energy is transferred by the current, but the current itself is charge flow, not energy flow.

C.explanation: An electron is one example of a charge carrier, not the flow itself.

D.explanation: Charge $Q$ on a particle is a static quantity in coulombs, whereas current is $I = Q/t$.
